newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares steady at open, seen higher later.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares steady at open, seen higher later.

text.p: Singapore shares opened little changed on Wednesday, stabilising after their sharp rise on Monday and downward correction on Tuesday.
But dealers said the market could rally later as it digested overnight gains on Wall Street and absorbed fresh demand from overseas institutions.
"I think some foreign funds see Singapore as good value," said one dealer. "I see demand for sectors like electronics."
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 0.48 higher at 2,251.27 by 0120 GMT on just over 50 million shares. Gainers led losers by 103 to 10.
Much of the early volume was in joinery products distributor Chuan Soon Huat, which soared 70 percent from its initial public offer price of Singapore $0.35 on debut to a high of S$0.595.
Twenty million shares in the firm changed hands in the first 20 minutes of trade. The price settled down later to S$0.565.
The biggest gainer of the early morning was computer sound card maker Creative Technology, which rose 40 cents to S$16.40.
Dealers said many electronics stocks were being re-rated.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 40.03 points overnight to yet another record high of 6,883.90.
